desc: Edwards Air Force Base covers 470 square miles of the western Mojave in Kern County, California, built around Rogers Dry Lake, an endorheic salt pan whose hard surface functions as a natural extension of the runways. It began in 1933 as the Muroc Bombing and Gunnery Range and was renamed in December 1949 for Capt. Glen Edwards, killed in the crash of the Northrop YB-49 flying wing. It hosts the Air Force Test Center, the U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School and NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center. Edwards is the acknowledged, white-world twin of Groom Lake: it is where American aircraft are flight tested when the government intends to admit they exist. That relationship is itself evidentiary. The CIA's own explanation for selecting Groom Lake in 1955 was explicit - flight test and pilot training for the U-2 could not be conducted at Edwards or at Lockheed's Palmdale facility given the extreme secrecy of the project. Edwards therefore defines the boundary condition: everything the United States is willing to acknowledge flies here, and the existence of a parallel unacknowledged test enterprise is established by the documented decision to move work away from this base. Edwards is also attached to one of the oldest and least substantiated claims in the field, the alleged February 1954 Muroc meeting between President Eisenhower and non-human occupants; the board records that claim as folklore with no primary record, and notes that its persistence has been useful to the concealment insofar as it makes the base's genuinely documented role harder to discuss seriously.
